title: Nightly Platform Review
description: Reads this platform's telemetry and agent conversations once a night and PROPOSES changes as pull requests. Applies nothing. Ships inert: dryRun true. REQUIRED BY core-provider, which derives the Composition CRD from this file.

global.title: Global values (injected by the Krateo composition engine)

jobDeadlineSeconds.description: activeDeadlineSeconds for each review Job. Must exceed config.agentAnalysis.totalSeconds plus the gather and the main ask. On expiry the run is recorded Failed, never left Running.

clickhouseQueries.title: Evidence queries
clickhouseQueries.description: Named SQL as configuration rather than code, so it is reviewable and adaptable without a new image. {from}/{to} are substituted as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' UTC; nothing else is, and a query without both is refused. The defaults aggregate over the schema Krateo writes (otel_logs; SeverityText is always empty here, so severity is matched in Body; Kubernetes events are ResourceAttributes['telemetry.source']='k8s-events' with the event as JSON in Body). A key set here replaces the default of that name.

default.errorPatternsByService:
SELECT ServiceName,
       ResourceAttributes['k8s.namespace.name'] AS ns,
       count() AS n
FROM otel_logs
WHERE Timestamp BETWEEN '{from}' AND '{to}'
  AND ResourceAttributes['telemetry.source'] = ''
  AND (position(Body, 'ERROR') > 0 OR position(Body, 'error') > 0
       OR position(Body, 'Failed') > 0 OR position(Body, 'panic') > 0)
GROUP BY ServiceName, ns
ORDER BY n DESC
LIMIT 25
default.kubernetesEventReasons:
SELECT JSONExtractString(Body, 'object', 'reason') AS reason,
       JSONExtractString(Body, 'object', 'kind')   AS kind,
       count() AS n
FROM otel_logs
WHERE Timestamp BETWEEN '{from}' AND '{to}'
  AND ResourceAttributes['telemetry.source'] = 'k8s-events'
  AND reason != ''
GROUP BY reason, kind
ORDER BY n DESC
LIMIT 25
default.logVolumeByService:
SELECT ServiceName, count() AS n
FROM otel_logs
WHERE Timestamp BETWEEN '{from}' AND '{to}'
GROUP BY ServiceName
ORDER BY n DESC
LIMIT 25

kagentDbHost.description: In-cluster address of kagent's Postgres. Reached directly and never through the gateway, because this is a database connection rather than an API call that per-user RBAC could be applied to.

targetCheckApiUrl.description: GitHub API base used to check that each proposal's target.repo exists (recorded as the TargetResolved condition; never a reason to drop a proposal). Anonymous unless config.targetCheck.tokenSecret names a credential; anonymously, a private repository answers 404 exactly like a missing one. Empty disables the check.

targetCheck.title: Authenticated existence check
targetCheck.description: A key of an EXISTING Secret, injected into the review pod as TARGET_CHECK_TOKEN by the kubelet (valueFrom.secretKeyRef, optional: true) and sent as `Authorization: Bearer` on the existence check's HEAD only. Needs no RBAC: the ServiceAccount still holds no Secret read. With it, a private repository the credential can see reads RepoFound, and a 404 reads RepoNotFound; a rejected credential (401) reads Unknown/CheckFailed. Never logged, never in a prompt or a status. An empty name disables it (anonymous check). NO SCHEMA DEFAULT, deliberately (core-provider would write it into the live composition spec); the chart's values.yaml sets {name: gh-token, key: token}. Absent means the anonymous check.

name.description: Secret in the release namespace. Empty disables.

key.description: Key in that Secret; the template uses `token` when empty.

targets.title: Fixed destinations per proposal kind
targets.description: kind (Alert, Widget, Prompt, Policy or Documentation; any other key is ignored) -> {repo, pathPrefix}. For a kind listed here the service REPLACES the model's target.repo, and the directory of target.path, before fingerprinting, and records each move in the run's ValidationNotes; the model keeps choosing the file name. The prompt tells the model these destinations are fixed. NO SCHEMA DEFAULT, deliberately: core-provider applies schema defaults into the live composition spec, so a default here would be a silent override. The chart's values.yaml sets Alert -> krateo-platformops/observability under charts/krateo-observability/templates. Wins over config.destinations (precedence: kind here > component in config.destinations.components > no destination). Absent, no kind is overridden. Helm merges maps: set a kind to add it, set Alert to null to drop it.

pathPrefix.description: Directory inside the repository; empty puts the file at the repository root. The directory never comes from the model.

destinations.title: Where proposals land, per component
destinations.description: THE ONLY SOURCE OF A PROPOSAL'S DESTINATION besides config.targets: the model's target.repo is never used. `components` maps a subject's component (the `component/` half, normalised like a subject: lowercase kebab) to {repo, pathPrefix, prompt}. A proposal about a listed component lands in `repo` under `pathPrefix`, keeping the model's file name; a Prompt proposal lands in prompt.repo at prompt.path exactly, and a component without `prompt` is no destination for one. Precedence: config.targets[kind] > components[component] > a blueprint's derived source repository (`blueprints`) > none. With none, target.repo is CLEARED, the proposal records TargetResolved False/NoDestination naming the component, and it is never published; it is still written, because the finding is real. NO SCHEMA DEFAULT at any depth, deliberately: core-provider applies schema defaults into the live composition spec. The chart's values.yaml seeds the platform's components, each verified to exist. Absent, every proposal not covered by config.targets records NoDestination. Helm merges maps: add a component by setting it, drop one with `<component>: null`.

components.description: component -> destination. Keys are normalised like a subject's component, so spell them as the evidence spells the component (a Deployment name, a ClickHouse ServiceName, a kagent agent name); a component seen under two spellings needs two keys.

repo.description: owner/name the component's source (or chart) lives in

pathPrefix.description: Directory a non-Prompt proposal's file lands in; empty puts it at the repository root.

prompt.description: Where this agent's system prompt lives, for Prompt proposals about it.

blueprints.description: Where a proposal about a BLUEPRINT lands when config.destinations.components does not list it: its source repository, derived each run from the chart URL of the CompositionDefinition that serves it (oci://ghcr.io/<org>/charts/<name> -> <org>/<name>, the release convention). Cluster data, never model output. Only for charts published by `orgs`; never for a Prompt proposal. TargetResolved still checks the repository exists. NO SCHEMA DEFAULT at any depth, deliberately: core-provider applies schema defaults into the live composition spec. Absent, nothing is derived.

orgs.description: GitHub orgs a blueprint's source repository may be derived in.

pathPrefix.description: Directory inside the blueprint's repository the proposal's file lands in; empty puts it at the repository root.

kagentQuestions.title: What people asked
kagentQuestions.description: Reads the text of USER-AUTHORED messages (never agent replies or tool output) from kagent sessions active in the review window, for every user, out of kagent's Postgres; redacted before it reaches the prompt. Requires SELECT on `event` for the secrets.kagentDb role. Bounded per session and in total, and every cut is recorded on the run. maxSessions 0 turns it off.

maxSessions.description: Most recently active conversations read. 0 disables the read.

maxMessagesPerSession.description: User messages read per conversation, oldest first inside the window.

maxCharsPerSession.description: Characters quoted per conversation, counted after redaction.

agentAnalysis.title: What the agents did
agentAnalysis.description: Between gather and ask, one model call per agent with conversations in the window, over those conversations IN FULL (user messages, agent replies, tool calls and tool results), window-bounded and redacted per message before any cut, with the agent's current system prompt read from its Agent object (promptTemplate include()s resolved from ConfigMaps). Only each call's bounded assessment reaches the main review, never a transcript, and this budget is separate from evidenceMaxChars. Same reviewer and same secrets.kagentDb role. Every cut is recorded on the run.

maxAgents.description: Agents analysed per run, most-used first; one model call each. Agents beyond it are recorded on the run as skipped (droppedAgents). 0 disables the stage.

maxSessionsPerAgent.description: Conversations read per agent, most recently active first.

maxMessagesPerSession.description: Stored events read per conversation: the first half and the last half, so the question and the outcome survive and the middle gives way.

maxCharsPerAgent.description: Characters of conversation shown for one agent, after redaction and every per-message cut. Separate from evidenceMaxChars: none of this reaches the main review.

maxCharsPerMessage.description: Characters per question, reply or error, after redaction.

maxToolResultChars.description: Characters per tool result, after redaction. The hard cap: tool results are the bulk of a conversation.

maxToolArgsChars.description: Characters of a tool call's arguments, after redaction.

maxPromptChars.description: Characters of the agent's resolved system prompt shown to the analysis; a longer prompt is cut and the run says so (promptTruncated).

maxEventChars.description: A stored event larger than this is not fetched from Postgres at all; its size is recorded as dropped.

timeoutSeconds.description: Total wall-clock budget for one agent's model call.

totalSeconds.description: Total budget for the whole stage. Agents not reached in time are recorded with the reason.

corpusMaxChars.description: What the assessments may add to the main review's corpus, all agents together.

excludeAgents.description: Globs over namespace/name or name. The reviewer this chart creates is always excluded too (its user turns are the previous night's corpus). Benchmark agents belong here: their traffic is a harness's, and product prompts must not be tuned from it.

promptConfigMaps.description: ConfigMap names, in this release's namespace, that Agents' promptTemplate dataSources may be read from. Empty grants get (never list) on ConfigMaps in this namespace only; naming them narrows the grant to exactly those resourceNames. Secrets are never granted: a systemMessageFrom Secret is recorded as not read.

syncStall.title: Resources out of sync for too long
syncStall.description: A deterministic check (no model): every kind the API serves in `groups` is listed (discovered at run time), and objects whose Synced condition is False (or, with no Synced verdict, Ready False for one of readyErrorReasons) for longer than thresholdMinutes by the condition's lastTransitionTime are grouped by component and failure pattern; each group is written as one Documentation Proposal under `<component>/<pattern>`, even when the model call fails. Secrets are named from *Ref fields, never read. A NIGHTLY BACKSTOP, not an alert. NO SCHEMA DEFAULT at any depth, deliberately: core-provider applies schema defaults into the live composition spec; values.yaml sets github.krateo.io and git.krateo.io. Absent or empty `groups` turns the check off.

thresholdMinutes.description: How long a condition must have been failing, by its lastTransitionTime, before it is reported.

groups.description: API group -> {component, kinds}. Helm merges maps: drop a seeded group with `<group>: null`.

component.description: The subject's component for this group's findings, spelled as config.destinations.components spells it, so the Proposal lands in that component's repository.

kinds.description: Kinds to check; empty checks every kind the group serves.

readyErrorReasons.description: Ready=False reasons that count as failing when there is no Synced verdict.

ignoreReasons.description: Synced=False reasons that are intent, not failure (a paused reconcile).

kagentDb.description: Credential for kagent's Postgres, read across every user: session METADATA and the text of user-authored messages (config.kagentQuestions), and — for config.agentAnalysis — whole conversations: agent replies, tool calls and tool results too. The role named here must hold SELECT on `session` and `event` and nothing else; it stays REVOKEd on `task`. No new grant is needed for the analysis: replies and tool output are rows of `event`, which the grant already covers — so the grant has never been what kept them out, and the scope each source records on the run says what it read. That narrowness is a database privilege, NOT something this chart enforces — verify it where the role is created (session=t, event=t, task=f). A role still revoked on `event` keeps the metadata and makes the run PartiallyCompleted. No `default` on any leaf here, deliberately: an empty name must mean not-configured so the source reports it and the run is PartiallyCompleted, rather than a default silently standing in.

portalAdminAccess.title: Portal admin access to proposals
portalAdminAccess.description: Binds a ClusterRole to these groups granting get/list/watch/patch on Proposals, get/list/watch on ReviewRuns and get/patch/update on proposals/status. `patch` on the main resource is how the portal records a decision (spec.decision), because snowplow /call cannot reach the status subresource; decisionPolicy is what keeps that patch to the decision alone. A binding rather than aggregate-to-admin: Krateo admins hold cluster-admin through their group, not the built-in admin ClusterRole, so aggregation would not reach them.

decisionPolicy.title: Admission policies on a proposal's decision
decisionPolicy.description: Ships a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that, for every requester other than this service's ServiceAccount, allows no spec change on a Proposal except spec.decision, forbids removing a decision or changing it other than PrOpen -> Rejected, and requires decidedBy to be the requesting user; and, where admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1 MutatingAdmissionPolicy is served (Kubernetes 1.36+), a MutatingAdmissionPolicy that stamps decidedBy and decidedAt from the request. Off leaves spec.decision unguarded: RBAC cannot narrow a patch to one field.
